MISC.label: Junk
MISC.summary: Loot dropped by monsters with no use but gold — body parts, hides, feathers, minerals, oddments. Sold at any shop.

SOUL.label: Soul Stone
SOUL.summary: A soul stone dropped by monsters — the card of one specific creature. Merged into a weapon or a piece of armor to grant it the stone's power; the stone is consumed by the merge. `one_per_monster` makes the binding STRICTLY 1-to-1: a stone is dropped by exactly one monster and a monster drops exactly one stone, so the wiki can show the creature on the stone and the stone on the creature. A stone with no monster yet is UNBOUND (it waits for one) — never a second stone on a monster that already has one.

monsters.name: Emberwing
monsters.lore: No bigger than a lantern, it drifts on wings too gaudy for a dragon — then breathes fire that shames its size.
monsters.loreDesc: Wings exact to the last scale, a lantern-sized dragon guessed at, and a jet of flame three times its length.
loreStory: No dragon was ever anywhere to be remembered. What there was, in a hundred countries at once, was the telling of one, and a telling said often enough, to enough people listening, weighs as much here as a life does. So this is not the memory of an animal; it is the memory of an account, and you can see the difference at ten paces. Whoever did most of the remembering had never seen a dragon — no one has — but they had lain in a summer meadow once, watching the irises being worked over close up, and when the account ran out, that is what came to hand. The wings are the best-made thing on it: four of them, violet banded with pink, exact to the last scale. The body is a grey-green guess the size of a lantern. What got looked at came out sharp. What got taken on trust came out approximate.

loreStory.t: Then it opens its mouth and puts out flame three times its own length, and the joke stops there. The fire is the one detail every retelling in every country kept, so it came through whole and unworn, entirely indifferent to the size of the thing carrying it.
Osric

, new enough to still count in living years, called it a moth with opinions, at a range he has since revised. The tellers do his eyebrows when they tell it, and he sits and lets them, which is most of why the fire likes him. Being wrong about a creature does not make it harmless. It only decides which parts of it are.
Bettany
keeps a page of dragon accounts in
the Chronicle
and cannot get two of the woken to agree on wings, size, colour, or where the hoard was kept. The page carries one sentence every hand has signed. The fire is right.

monsters.name: Nightmule
monsters.lore: A pack beast gone feral in the dark, white-eyed and stubborn. It charges head-first and will not be reasoned with.
monsters.loreDesc: Unharnessed, unloaded, unled — and still keeping to its route. Get in the way and it comes on at a walk.
loreStory: In the life it fell out of, somebody owned it. That is worth knowing, because of what comes off one: a bronze camp knife, hemp rope chewed to a splay, three iron links worn smooth on the inside by years of harness, a roll of coarse grey canvas. One person's kit for going somewhere and stopping for the night, all of it still coming off an animal that is carrying nothing at all.

loreStory.t: It keeps a route. It comes on at a walk, in a line, and the line does not bend around you, because you are standing in a road it was walking before the road went soft.
Wendell
swears the line is the old east road, and for an evening's company he will name you every stop on it — which is one more thing than the animal can do.

loreStory: The load went. The voice up at the front went so long ago there is no name left to put to it. Now and then it halts in open ground, swings both ears forward at nothing whatever, waits to be spoken to, and then walks on.

monsters.name: Ashfiend
monsters.lore: A thin horror with too many eyes and no patience. It strikes with its skull and falls to ash when finished.
monsters.loreDesc: A crowned bone face, two sizes too big for the starved body carrying it. Fights head-first. Goes to ash.
loreStory: It does not walk. It gathers both feet under itself and crosses the ground in bounds, and it takes you crown-first, head down, the hardest thing left on it leading. Nothing that ever hunted for a living fights with its face. And it hurries. Everything empty in the open country has all the time there is; this one moves like something with an errand, and the errand is not its own.

loreStory.t: What comes off one is mostly not its own either. Grey talons of the kind the lit thing sheds. Hooks sized for a big cat's mouth. On
Sigrun
's bench last autumn, out of a head with two red eyes, a whole wet eye, brown.
Osric
, new enough to still ask things out loud, asked what it wanted the eye for. Sigrun tied the bag and put it with the others. Everyone in the room understood the answer except him.
Broken, it folds at the knees and settles, and the settling is ash; the wind has the heap by morning, near
the mouth
as anywhere. It leaves no mask. The face goes with the rest of it — it only goes last.

monsters.name: Balefiend
monsters.lore: Elder kin of the eye-demons, wreathed in flame and swirling dark. Its slam is meant to crush, not to wound.
monsters.loreDesc: Nothing behind the face — four slit eyes burning in black stone, wreathed in dark. Its attack is to fall on you.
loreStory: A face of black stone, four slit eyes lit orange down it, red marks cut above and below them, the whole thing hanging inside a wreath of slow dark that takes fire when it moves. It does not strike. It rises, and it comes down on you with everything it weighs, meaning to crush. And the eyes shut first — all four, a breath before the stone cracks — so whatever was doing the looking is gone before the breaking starts.

loreStory.t: There are two accounts of it and neither has won. One: it is a shell the emptying made when it had nothing left to work with, the outside done beautifully, the inside not attempted. The other: it is one of the masks, left lying too long near
the mouth
, and no longer an object. The crackers prefer the first. The second has a next question in it.
Jehanne

was sent a rubbing of the red marks, on the reasoning that a priestess reads things. She kept it through a winter. In spring she burned it, and told the sender the marks say nothing at all — in the voice she keeps for the prayers she no longer believes. She has not gone east since.

monsters.name: Dewling
monsters.lore: A pale meadow blob that balances a dewdrop like a crown — and swings it at whatever wanders too close.
monsters.loreDesc: Round and sand-pale, balancing one bright drop on a stalk. The drop is the weapon and comes round like a flail.
loreStory: The collectors call all the round ones lings, one word for the same business turning up in five kinds of country, and the low country's is pale as dry sand, holding a single bright drop up over itself on a stalk. Of everything a wet field at first light contains, the drop on its stem with the sun inside is the detail everyone keeps exactly; the rest wears down under all that remembering to pale grain, no particular grass, no particular year.

loreStory.t: It swings the drop round like a weight on a line, catching the light as it comes, meaning none of it. The trade's one rule is to work with the sun at your back, because whoever is looking into the flash when the blow lands loses the next few steps of the fight. Flattened, it leaves no body at all, just
something sun-bleached and far too heavy
lying in the pressed grass.
Most mornings one comes partway up the rise toward the fire on
the meadow where everyone wakes
and stops just short of the light, and the fire's oldest joke is that it has come to be met.
Solveig

lets the joke stand. But after a night when the fire sat ready and the meadow stayed empty, she has been seen walking down the wet field to stand beside it a while, and whatever she says there she has never once brought back up the hill.

monsters.name: Sprigling
monsters.lore: A green woodland blob armed with a splinter of oak. Cut it down and it scatters into smaller blobs.
monsters.loreDesc: Green, damp, a shoot coming up out of its head, and a little wooden sword in a fist it does not really have.
loreStory: The wood's ling is green and damp, with a live shoot coming up out of its head. A wood, to nearly everyone who ever remembered one, is a place you went into to take something out of, and the stroke is the part that comes back identical from every rememberer — so it carries a small pale-wood sword out of nowhere in particular and swings it at travellers and passing birds with the same blank willingness. No grudge; there is nothing in it that could hold one.

loreStory.t: Osric

burns charcoal at the wood's edge, and in his first month here — he still said weeks then, as if weeks were load-bearing — one walked its round through his camp every day and swung at him every time. What offended him was not the swinging but the grip. He stopped dodging, took the little fist it does not really have, and set the sword properly in it, the way you set an apprentice's. It struck him anyway. He maintains it struck better.
Broken, it is chips before you can regret it, small green pieces in all directions at once, and what stays behind is
a stone with black grain run through it like sawn timber

. Osric buys those from the woodcutters. His own one still comes through the camp, and he has moved the woodpile out of its road, and he does not say what he will do on the morning the round comes through empty.

monsters.name: Quillkin
monsters.lore: A grumpy ball of needles that would rather nap than fight. Corner it and the quills leave first, fast as arrows.
monsters.loreDesc: Still laying in stores for a hand that stopped coming. Crowd this brown handful of spines and the quills stay in.
loreStory: It travels the bottoms of things — walls, hedge-lines, the low sides of paths — on a route that stopped leading anywhere long ago, carrying a fistful of hard glossy kernels it cannot eat and will not be parted from. A hedgehog has no use for a nut. Behind this one was a person who put food out at a certain hour, and an animal that learned to be at the place when they did, and of that whole arrangement the piece that lasted is the being-there. It still arrives at the old hour, to a patch of grass where a doorstep used to be, and waits, and eats nothing, and moves on.

loreStory.t: Wendell

says the wall it keeps to on the old east road was a garden wall, and that he knows whose garden. He is not making it up; the road is his stock in trade, and he sells what he remembers of it for company. So the name this animal has been keeping its appointment with is not gone. It is sitting in an old man by a fire, one evening's listening from being said aloud, and nobody has paid the evening yet.

Crowd it and the quills go in barbed and stay in. Somewhere in the dark there is a black-pelted thing carrying three of them, from a meeting on the low side of a path that neither of them chose or understood. The
white rabbit
keeps an hour of its own, out on open ground. The low country is full of them.

monsters.name: Rimeshard
monsters.lore: Black rock grown through with living ice. It tears crystal spears from the ground and swings them like clubs.
monsters.loreDesc: Dark rock grown through with ice: a crown, a mouthful, bladed arms, and more torn out of the ground at need.
loreStory: Above the snow line the ground turns crystal and stays that way, and the Rimeshard is what that ground does to a rock that stands in it long enough: dark plates iced through, a crown of blades off the skull, a mouth that is a row of them. When it wants more than it is wearing, it reaches down and tears it out of the ground — up there it and the ground are the same material, and there has never once been a shortage.

So the trade keeps one rule about it, bought dear and given away free: never above the line. Baited downhill onto ground that is merely ground, it spends its crown, then its shoulders, and cannot reach for more, and a patient crew can break the shape by dark. Above the line you are not fighting a creature so much as the ground it stands on, and the ground goes down a long way further than your patience.

loreStory.t: Ask
Hearn
what was under
the mountain

and he goes somewhere behind his own face. Ask him instead about the Rimeshard he passed on the trail down and he will talk all evening: how it marked him, and let him by, and wanted nothing, took nothing, asked him for nothing. He calls it the most restful thing on that whole road. People who work the high ground use the same word, restful — and use it, as a rule, in the season before they come down for good.

monsters.name: Frostling
monsters.lore: A snow-packed blob with a frozen grin. It spits ice spikes, and melts to slush when its winter finally ends.
monsters.loreDesc: Packed snow with two dark eyes, heavier than snow should be. Every spike it throws is grown out of itself.
loreStory: Down in the grass the ground wanders; high under the crystal country nothing has needed correcting in a very long time, and there is hardly anyone left up there to walk on it. Out of ground held that hard comes the high snow's ling: snow pressed into a shape with two dark eyes, far heavier than snow has any business being, and armed entirely out of itself. A spike grows up through its crown and flies, and there is measurably less creature afterwards. It will do that until it cannot.

loreStory.t: Gunnar

goes up each year to check his measurements of the Drift against the one country that never moves, and each year the same one — the eyes set a little crooked; you learn one the way you learn a face — meets him at the last ridge and throws everything it has. He stands out of range and lets it finish. His is the only footfall on that road all year. Whatever it is armed against, he is the whole of what ever arrives.

loreStory: It is smaller each year. He measures it — he measures everything — and keeps the number where he keeps the rest, to himself. They do not shatter at the end; they slump, into slush inside their own footprint, and the wet mark outlasts them by an hour. Gunnar says that the year it does not throw at him, he will retire the route. He says it the way he says most things, so that you cannot tell whether it is a joke.

monsters.name: Slagling
monsters.lore: A crust of cooled stone with molten rage beneath. It flares white-hot when angered, then melts into slag.
monsters.loreDesc: Under a crust of cooled rock, a fistful of heat going out. To strike, it splits along the seams and flares.
loreStory: A stretch of the black rock is the wrong colour and warm through the boot, and things get up out of ground argued over that hard. What everyone keeps of a fire is not the flame: it is the black skin that forms over a late log with the red still moving underneath. So that is what stood up — the black rock's ling, a fistful of banked heat in a shell of cooled stone, going out from the moment it got up.

It fights by splitting. The seams open, the flare comes all at once, the shell shuts, and there is a little less inside than there was. You cannot hurry one in any way that is not ugly, so the workers up there walk beside it instead and let it spend itself, and by evening it is down to its last light.

loreStory.t: Jehanne
found one guttering above the tree line on a
rota
walk and did what she does at every failing fire on her list: knelt and fed it, stick by stick, half the night, into seams that could not take wood. It went out toward morning anyway. She carries
the ember it left
unsold in her rota coat, and when
Bettany
asked her, for the Chronicle, why she had fed a thing she knew was not a fire, she gave the answer she gives about the evening prayers: the practice was never for the fire.

monsters.name: Emberjaw
monsters.lore: Basks in cooling magma and bites with a mouthful of flame. Its hide stays warm for hours after it falls.
monsters.loreDesc: Basks all day, crusted and cracked open on the light beneath, then gets up breathing fire it never learned.
loreStory: What fell was small: a damp thing the length of a hand, bark-coloured, living under wet wood, no danger to anything and in none itself. What basks on the black rock now stands several times that — hide gone to crust, the crust split along its seams on a steady light, and when the mouth opens, fire comes out. A great many of the dead once put a log on a fire and watched a little creature run out of the flame; every one of them drew the obvious conclusion, and not one went back and checked. When the animal's own account of itself wore thin, their story is what was left holding the shape.

loreStory.t: It spends the day flat on the warm stone, doing just what the story says it should, then gets up and walks a round nothing accounts for and bites whatever is standing in it — and the fire makes the bite the smaller half of the problem.
Jehanne
walks out once a season to look at it. She keeps a rite she stopped believing because people need the fire either way, and she says this creature is her whole argument, standing up and warm.
The coal it finally comes down to
does not cool
. The black rock runs on toward the cave, warmer the whole way, and the creature walks to the edge of that ground and turns back, every time.

monsters.name: Palemaw
monsters.lore: A pale cave-dweller with a jaw built for bone. It bites once, hard, and seldom needs to bite twice.
monsters.loreDesc: Dull olive, pale flat eyes, a gape wider than the skull carrying it. One bite. Rarely two.

loreStory.t: The Chronicle
files it beside
the burning one

because at forty paces they share a silhouette, and there the resemblance ends. Nothing about this animal is lit. It is lichen-olive going grey, the eyes flat, pale and wrong, and the head is mostly jaw — hinged so far back that the gape opens wider than the skull carrying it. It gives no warning at all. One bite, and generally that is the encounter.

What it hunts is the hard things. Bone first — it will spend a night on one marrow bone and leave it knobbed and stained in the open, which is how you know one is working an area — then stone, and gold whenever it finds any, though no one has ever opened one and found gold inside. It works ground nearer the cave than anything else that still has an inside.
Hearn
will guide a cracker as far as the chewed bones and no farther; he waits there facing the mountain, and he does not sit down.
The paws it sheds are never a matching pair: what grows back after a loss comes back approximate, and the next one approximate from the approximation. The hard piece in the jaw is
sea-green, mended through with gold
; what the mend means is an argument for the people who trade it. The animal goes on taking what refuses to go, and has never once looked like it wondered why.

monsters.name: Palehusk
monsters.lore: Someone's failed experiment, wearing borrowed skin. It shambles after travellers on limbs that bend wrongly.
monsters.loreDesc: Bare, blotched, hairless and shaped exactly like a person, coming at a walk with one hand open and green.
loreStory: Out on the warm black rock, exactly the shape of a person, bare and blotched and wearing nothing. What tells you at fifty paces is the arms: a walking person's arms swing, and these hang. It follows, and it does not hurry, and when it arrives it does not bite and does not claw. It reaches — one open hand, out and across, green standing in the seams of it, a gesture anybody would recognise. Everyone who has met one says the gesture is the worst part.

It kept things. A bronze locket grown in under the skin of its chest. A pitted silver ring on a finger it was never made for. Grave dirt in the creases. The ones who go through what a broken one leaves are not robbing it, they are reading it, and no name has ever been read off one.

loreStory.t: Hearn
went into
the cave
with the one organised attempt anyone ever made on it, and came out alone, and in all the years since has said exactly one thing about the inside: it asked politely. Last winter at
Solveig
's fire, a cracker fresh off the black rock was describing the open hand. Hearn stood up, and asked which hand, and went out. He has not added anything since.

monsters.name: Diretusk
monsters.lore: A mountain of dark wool and ivory, calm until crowded. One sweep of those tusks clears a road.
monsters.loreDesc: Crowd it and one sweep of ivory clears the road. Otherwise it grazes, wool to the ankles, a herd of one.
loreStory: Nothing else grazing this country comes near it for size: wool to the ankles, a shoulder above a grown person's head, ivory curved out far enough to clear a road. It is not hunting anything and never was. Nearly everything that has ever gone wrong between one of these and a person happened because the person stood too close for too long — the head comes round, one sweep, and the conversation is over.

loreStory.t: Watch the spacing instead. It keeps a gap open on either side of itself, and it halts the way an animal halts when the animal ahead has halted. There is no animal ahead.
Gunnar
, who shares his measurements with no one, still marks the one on his eastern round as a fixed point, the way other maps use hills — the hills out there having proved less dependable.
Bringing one down takes the knees first, then a long settling into the grass, and what is left fits in a closed hand:
a piece of ivory webbed with hairline breaks

. Every one of them is a break it kept walking after — the tusks it sheds are snapped clean at the root by things it never once broke stride for. What the piece lends whoever carries it is exactly what the animal had. Not strength. The habit of continuing while damaged.

monsters.name: Grinmask
monsters.lore: A sliver of living dark behind a grinning mask. Slay it and the shadow is gone; the mask clatters down, still smiling.
monsters.loreDesc: Not a thing that thinned — a thing that was emptied. What falls when it breaks is a mask, and the masks all match.
loreStory: Everything else out there is running on habit — a shape walking its round with the details gone, that will only hurt you for standing in the round. Grinmask stops when you stop and starts when you start. It plays. Crackers who work the eastern ground will take any two of anything else before one of these, because the rest defend themselves and this one has intentions, and the intentions did not come from the shape.

loreStory.t: Break it and the dark is simply not there any more — no struggle, no leaving. What comes down is the mask, and the mask does not thin.
Bettany

drew one for the Chronicle, and two winters later drew another, off a beast broken thirty miles from the first. She laid the new tracing over the old: line onto line, the whole way round. The same face. Smiling, both times — they are always smiling. And the inward side is smooth as a bowl. Not a face something wore. A face something made.
Those two drawings are most of the reason there is an
investigation
at all. Bettany, who has interviewed half the country about the worst day of its life without flinching, keeps both masks face-down in a drawer now, and has stopped drawing them.

monsters.name: Mirewart
monsters.lore: Fattened on swamp-magic and far too clever. Novices laugh at it once, then learn to respect the slam.
monsters.loreDesc: A green weight in the shallows, in no hurry to move, and the first live thing this country shows its newly woken.

loreStory.t: Animals fall into this country too, and no one meets them; there is nothing useful anyone can say to a frog. This one has held the shallows at the low end of the meadow since before the roads were where they are, working the only trade it knows: sit where the flies come, hold still, be patient. The low wet ground is where
the newly woken

drift while they still cannot say their own names, so the first live thing this world shows a great many people is a green weight with a hard yellow eye on each side of its head, looking back and not getting up.
Wendell

woke when the east road was still safe and could not find his name for three days, and got it back sitting in that mud, saying pieces of it to the frog — because you can say a name wrong to a frog, and say it wrong again, and it asks nothing back. He has traded the story for company at fires ever since. Last spring
Osric
came up from those same shallows with wet boots and the same story, and Wendell will not hear a word about it being a different frog.
It is also, often, the first thing the frightened ones break: it is close, it is slow, it does not run. The small warm stone it leaves
sets quietly to work
closing the knuckles of the very hand that did it. So Wendell gives every one of the newly woken he can catch the same advice: go down and tell the frog your name. It will not care. That is the gift.

monsters.name: Glowbone
monsters.lore: Its bones burn through split hide, lighting the woods it hunts. You see the glow long before the claws.
monsters.loreDesc: Dark hide split at the shoulders and spine, lit bone standing up through it. You see one coming a long way off.

loreStory.t: On all fours, hunched, arms too long and ending in fingers, the hide split along the shoulders and spine with lit bone standing up through the splits. The keepers of the old eastern circuit called it the last mercy near
the mouth
: the one thing out there that cannot cross a black wood without announcing itself.
Wendell
walked that circuit young, and will still trade you the saying, along with everything else he remembers of the east, for an evening's company.
Gunnar

will not sit through that particular evening any more. Gunnar watched one hunt. The light stood up out of its ribs at a creature that had lived in the dark long enough to give up on light, and the creature stayed exactly where it was, blind, while the long arm arrived. The light is not leaking, and it was never a mercy. It is the part that does the work.

Breaking one goes wrong in a particular way: it comes apart at the neck, the lit head leaves first, and the rest stands up on its hands a moment longer — the part everyone reaches in the telling and then skips. The light does not go down with it.
The piece it leaves
is still burning, and not one hour of all that burning, out in all that dark, was ever lit for anybody.

monsters.name: Duskfang
monsters.lore: A shadow-furred hunter out of an older age. It runs down what it wants and ends the argument in one bite.
monsters.loreDesc: A hunter left over from an age this country stopped telling, black-furred, amber-eyed, built for one rush.
loreStory: The fangs are longer than the mouth can shut over, so the jaw has to open the whole way before they are any use, and by then you are out of choices. It lies in open grass for hours doing nothing, calm the way a cat is calm — not calm at all, a decision that has not been taken yet. Then the whole animal happens at once. It was built for one rush, and there is no account anywhere of a second.

It came down out of an age so far back that everyone who woke remembering it has since thinned or gone on, so it never comes up at the fires. Untold things go in order: the plain went first, then the weather on the plain, then the others of its kind, strung out along the line of a hunt. What is left in the grass is the last hundred yards of one.

loreStory.t: Bettany

asked at four fires for one story about it and got blank looks, which frightened her more than the animal did. So she walked out, sat a careful distance from one for a day, and wrote what she saw into
the Chronicle
— noting in the margin that being looked at is not the same as being told about. It is the only entry in her book with no teller behind it.

monsters.name: Frostwraith
monsters.lore: Gaunt, winged and starving in the drifts. Its ice-claws leave frost-burned wounds that are slow to close.
monsters.loreDesc: Gaunt, four-horned, snow to the claws. The wings never beat. Two colours on it are wrong, and both are hot.
loreStory: Snow-coloured from the crest to the claws, so the first thing anybody sees of one is its eyes. It comes on its feet, wings held open and never once beaten, and makes no sound at all on the snow, and it does not stop hunting, because there is almost nothing up there to catch and nothing in it that could ever be full. What the claws open does not close; the cold moves into the wound and settles.

loreStory.t: The trouble is not what it is. The trouble is where it is. The high snow lies a great many days uphill, on the far side of the massif from
the mouth
, over country more of the dead have agreed on, for longer, than any other ground in the world. People called it safe on exactly that reasoning: too well remembered to lose.
Gunnar

came down off that country in spring with his survey unfinished, which no one had known him to do. He had found talon sockets in the drift, ragged, in matched sets, a whole season's line of them, and he had taken a bearing along the line. The sockets are on his map now. The bearing he keeps where he keeps most of what the ground has been doing lately — to himself — and the people who trust Gunnar's silences have started going the long way west.

monsters.name: Mosscairn
monsters.lore: Moss-clad boulders bound by old earth-magic. It rips the ground open with one fist; the head topples first.
monsters.loreDesc: A cairn that got up. Moss on every weathered face, a flat head low in the shoulders, one fist that opens ground.
loreStory: Every field anybody ever worked was cleared first, and every cleared field kept its heap: rounded brown stones at the edge of the ground, added to a little each season, walked around for a lifetime, never once taken from. Enough of that, in enough fields, and one of the heaps has a face in it. Add to it and welcome — travellers still set a stone on its shoulder in passing, the way you would on any cairn, and it takes no notice. Take from it, even one stone, and you meet the fist. A heap only ever grew. Being taken from is the thing that was never done to it.

loreStory.t: People chance the fist anyway, because in the fall of a broken one there is sometimes raw
gold
, and a pocket of gold buys a great deal of nerve.
Wendell

refuses to call that a fair trade. On the old east road there is a Mosscairn carrying, third down from the crown, a flat grey stone he set there himself — one trip a year, forty years of trips, back when the road was safe and he still walked it. His waymark is out there yet, riding the shoulder of a thing that walks a road he no longer dares. Bring him word of where it stands now and he will sit you down at his fire until you have heard the whole road, mile by mile, the way it was.

monsters.name: Magmashell
monsters.lore: Ancient, grumpy, and full of banked fire. The cracks in its shell glow brighter the angrier it gets.
monsters.loreDesc: Hot stone in a tortoise's shape, orange banked in every seam. Still keeping a crossing that stopped being used.
loreStory: Of the ways over the gorge, one is no longer taken. The path up to it went elsewhere in a Turn, the walk round came out shorter than the climb, and the crossing has carried nothing but weather since. The tortoise on it was never posted there. For a long stretch of years, everyone who described a high crossing also described what waits on one — something old, something slow, something you do not argue with — and when this crossing emptied, all that describing had nowhere left to live. It came up out of the ground into the gap and took the post.

There is a toll, and the toll is a pause. Stop at the edge of its span, stand still for the length of a slow breath, and it swings its bulk aside and lets you over. Try to save the breath and the seams come up bright from tail to skull, and by then it is generally too late to have wanted the other route.

loreStory.t: Gunnar
pays the pause twice a year, in both directions, the only regular the crossing has left. A crossing that carries no one, he says, goes in the end
the way of anything untold

, and a man who maps the Drift wants one fixed thing to measure from. That is what he says. His measurements he keeps to himself, and the walk round, people have begun to notice, comes out a little longer every year.

monsters.name: Stumpling
monsters.lore: A stump that woke one spring. It hauls itself along on root-legs and lashes at anyone who treads on its moss.
monsters.loreDesc: A stump with no tree behind it, walking on root-legs. It does not mind you coming. It minds you leaving.
loreStory: Every village that ever was had one: the stump at the wood's edge where you walked people to say goodbye. You carried their bag that far and no farther, and they sat on it to retie a boot, and then they went, and you stood by the stump until you could not see them. A thousand villages, a hundred thousand goodbyes, all of them remembered hard by the people left standing there — and in Nangijala that much remembering, pooled in one shape, eventually stands up.

So mind the one thing every handler tells you and no field guide bothers to: a Stumpling will let you walk right up. It goes for your back. The lashing starts when you turn and go, because going is the only thing that was ever done to it, and somewhere in all that borrowed remembering it has decided, wordlessly, with nobody inside it to decide, that this time it will not be left.

loreStory.t: Sigrun
will not crack them. She does the trade's other work all day and charges double to anyone who brings her one of these still whole, hoping she'll change her mind. The stone inside is
blood-natured

— it feeds your wounds shut while you fight, holding on to you the way the stump holds on to everyone — and she says a thing that keeps its grip that well should be allowed to keep it. People assume she is joking. People have not watched her leave her smithy, at the end of a market day, by the long way around the one that stands at the east fence.

monsters.name: Puddling
monsters.lore: A wobbling drop of pond water with a face. Cornered it bursts; beaten, it spreads out and quietly steams away.
monsters.loreDesc: Two big eyes in a wobble of pond water. Corner it and it bursts into spray, then gathers itself back up.
loreStory: No creature drowned to make the ponds' one. A low wet place got remembered by a great many people and visited by none of them, and the remembering pooled the way water pools, and one morning it had a face. Fight it and it bursts — alarming exactly once — sits a moment as a flat wet patch, and is a blob again before you have decided how you feel about that. Nothing lands. There is nothing in it to land on.

loreStory.t: The sorters' first question for any wild thing — what has it lost? — goes nowhere here, which is exactly why
Bettany

carried her whole list down to the pond and put every question to one aloud, in order, while it wobbled and watched her. It burst once, when a heron came down, and was back before she had finished the next question. Under its page in
the Chronicle
she wrote: stayed to the end of the questions, which is more than most people do. She maintains that this was an observation.
The pond, for what it is worth, has not moved since. Two Turns have been through the low country and left it exactly where her page says it is.
Gunnar
marks it on his maps as the stillest water in the district and, being Gunnar, will not say why he thinks so.

monsters.name: Fluffang
monsters.lore: Harmless-looking and quick to bolt, though the bite is real. A beginner's first honest mistake.
monsters.loreDesc: Tame in a way nothing wild is: it comes closer than it should, bolts, and bites in earnest when it cannot run.
loreStory: White is a poor colour in country that has things hunting in it, and the coat is not the strange part. The strange part is that it comes toward you. Nothing wild does that. A rabbit has decided in advance about every noise there is, and this one decides right about all of them, and then for a moment decides wrong: three or four steps in your direction, ears up, the way an animal moves toward a person it is expecting — then whatever is left inside catches up with it, and it is forty feet away. Somebody kept this one. The somebody got forgotten before the rabbit did.

loreStory.t: Twice a day it comes out onto the same patch of open ground within sight of
the meadow
, faces the same way, and waits. Nothing arrives.
Solveig

can see the spot from the fire, and when the fire can spare her she goes and sits at it — a little way off, at the hour, saying nothing. It will not take food from her; she is the wrong person, and it knows that better than it knows anything. She goes anyway. She has met strangers at their worst hour her whole watch, and she says a kept hour should not have to be kept alone.

loreStory: It will not turn while it still has somewhere to run. Take that away and it turns, and the teeth were always real. Most first seasons include this lesson, the gentlest on offer: nearly everything in this country will hurt you eventually, and almost none of it means to.

characters.name: Man
characters.lore: A young man of the human race — no claws, no scales, no magic in the blood, just nerve and a quick pair of hands. He sets out with nothing but what he stands in.
characters.loreDesc: Newly woken on the meadow with his name still on him, which is rarer than it sounds. What he was is over; what he will be has not been decided yet.

loreStory.t: He woke in the meadow grass with his name still on him, which is rarer than it sounds, and
Solveig

was beside him before the dew had soaked through his shirt. She told him the truth once, plainly, and asked his name and one true thing. The name came easily. The true thing took him until sundown — it was small, and she thanked him for it as if he had paid a debt, because here a true thing said aloud is exactly that.

loreStory: He still checks his pockets for something he last had on the other side. They are empty. So were everyone's — arriving with nothing is the one experience this whole country shares, and it is why a stranger here will feed you before you ask.

There is nothing remarkable about him, and this is not modesty: quick hands, a stubborn streak he had before the end, and no idea yet what either is for. Solveig is unworried. The ones who thank her, she says, always turn up at the meadow again sooner or later — on the far side of the courtesy, walking out into the wet grass to meet somebody new.

characters.name: Woman
characters.lore: A young woman of the human race, level-headed and hard to rattle. She carries no blade yet, only the stubborn confidence that carried humankind this far.
characters.loreDesc: Newly woken and hard to rattle. She had most of it worked out by the second evening, and has not yet said how she feels about any of it.
loreStory: She woke and took it better than most, which she is aware is a strange thing to be good at. By her second evening she had worked the rest out unassisted: that the fire was kindness rather than answers, and that the people being kind were not going to explain the important part, because they do not know it either. She has asked good questions ever since, and has not once asked whether it is really true.

loreStory.t: Bettany

came out from the stone house on her third morning, book open, the way she comes for everyone who will sit. The woman answered every question and then asked better ones back, which does not usually happen, and Bettany stayed past noon writing those down too. The last question, the gentle one — who she is waiting for — she was slowest to answer. What she said is not in the Chronicle; Bettany had already closed the book.

loreStory: What she is, is hard to rattle. Not brave the way the tellers mean it when they are working a room — brave in the flat, unremarkable way of somebody who looks at a thing that should be frightening, decides how frightened to be, and is then that frightened and no more. Everybody in this country is waiting for something. She has not said what. She will get around to it.

loreStory.t: The forge came before the grief could. He woke recently enough that the living country is still the country to him: he counts in living years, and will tell you mid-hammer that his daughter turns nine this winter —
the Human Dead

has that scene, and the loud hour that follows it. What it does not have is the shelf above his bench, where a ninth-winter gift already sits finished, months early, wrapped in oilcloth: a little iron horse with a mane he filed for a week, waiting on a delivery no smith can make.

He is waiting too. His wife went three winters ahead of him, and by his arithmetic she should have been standing in the meadow grass to meet him. So he walks the meadow's edge every morning before the forge is lit, and reads the grass, and comes back, and works.
The Waking

is honest about arithmetic like his. Twice now somebody at the fire has begun the sentence — some of the dead never — and both times the hammer came down on iron that did not need it. The sentence has stayed unfinished in his presence ever since, and people let him have that. Winter is long.
Sigrun

is taking the living words off him one at a time — he calls her the best teacher he never asked for — and she, who corrects everything, has left that sentence alone. Once, over the quenching trough, he asked her how long a person can decently wait. She let the steel stop singing first. As long as you keep the fire fed, she said. He took it for encouragement. It was not quite that.

loreStory.t: What was left of her husband walked. A
Habit

shape runs one faithful loop, empty of anyone; his ran the roads he had walked home by all his life, and it ended at her door, and stood there, and did not knock. She let it stand the first time. By the third she understood what a shape on open road is to any stranger with a good eye and a day to spare. So she opened the door and let him finish arriving — all the way in, all the way home — and broke the shape herself, at the hearth, with the doors shut.
The hammer she uses now she made in the days between — a new head with a socket sunk in it, sized to a
stone

she did not yet hold. Practical people grieve forward. What rides in that socket is the trade's favourite story and not one she tells; what she will do is pass the finished blade across hilt-first and watch how it gets taken. Some people receive a sword. Some people take one. She has lifted a blade back out of a buyer's grip and returned the gold without explanation, and the trade has learned not to ask.
She has taken on the new blacksmith's education, unasked.
Osric

arrived weeks-woken with the living word for breaking things still in his mouth, and she took it off him inside a month — not by correcting him, but by making him watch her work until the wrong word embarrassed itself. He calls her the best teacher he never asked for. As for the name she has not said since that day at the hearth: it is not in this record, it is not in the Chronicle, and it is not going to be. She is not keeping it from anyone. She is keeping it.

characters.name: Solveig
characters.lore: Solveig, a townsfolk of Nangijala. One of Nangijala's own — no armour, no title, just a life being got on with.
characters.loreDesc: Keeper of the meadow fire, the first face the newly woken see. She finished a shift once that should have broken her, and has kept every one since.

loreStory.t: The watch was handed to her. She learned it from the woman before her — the seat with its back to the wind, the second cup in case a waking came thirsty, the courtesy word for word — and she loved her, in the unannounced way of a thousand shared quiet nights. One night, mid-vigil, mid-story — an old tale from the living country that Solveig had heard forty times and never once to the end, because something always interrupted — the voice went
Quiet

between one word and the next, and the bench was empty, and the fire wanted feeding. Solveig fed it. She kept the watch to sunrise and met the morning's waking with a level voice. Then she walked out past the woodpile and cried until the sun was high.
Her name was Tove. It is in
the Chronicle
because Solveig went to
Bettany

the week after and stood over the page until every letter was down. And she still tells the unfinished story at the fire, exactly as far as it goes, and asks everyone she meets there, once the shaking stops, whether they knew that tale in life. Somebody crossed over knowing the ending. One evening somebody will wake in that grass carrying it, and she means to be sitting there when they do.

loreStory: She could go on any evening — she is as whole as anyone left — and everyone knows what she says about staying: if she goes, who meets them? What she does not say is that Tove could have gone once too, and stayed for the same reason, and stayed past the going. Solveig stands in a door she watched close on the woman before her, and stands there anyway, on purpose. Ask how long she has kept the watch and you get the answer Tove used to give: since morning.

characters.lore: Wendell, a village elder of Nangijala. Old enough to remember the last bad winter and mean it as a warning.
characters.loreDesc: Elder of the meadow fire. He pays for company with the east road, one evening at a time, and knows better than anyone how much road he has left.

loreStory.t: The oldest head at the meadow fire pays his way in road. What he sells — the carts, the inn at the ford, the summer the verge came up in flowers — and where he walks when the weather is quiet, and beside whom, is told in
the Quiet

, and told right. What that chapter is too kind to add: a telling keeps the east road firm under feet that still walk it, so every evening he sells is maintenance, and every listener who thinks they are indulging an old man is holding up a road without knowing whose.

Last winter he caught himself putting the flowers in the wrong summer. A small slip, the kind any teller makes — except that everyone who could have corrected him is gone, and the road is now exactly as true as his remembering, no truer. He finished the story, said nothing, and began a private tally that night: which stretch, sold to whom, how often, what he no longer trusts.
Bettany
has the whole road saved, forty pages, milestone by milestone; for her evenings he trades a different memory altogether, a thread a week, and knows exactly what he is doing.

loreStory: Ask why a man that old and that whole has never gone on, and you will be paid in road stories. The true answer walks a fixed stretch at a fixed hour and holds only while somebody keeps saying carts, ford, flowers. He does not name her, and neither will this book. He is running out of road and running out of evenings, and he has already decided, telling no one, which of the two of them gets the last of it.

characters.name: Hearn
characters.lore: Hearn, a grizzled veteran of Nangijala. Too old for the front rank, too stubborn to say so. Carries knives where the young carry hope.
characters.loreDesc: Veteran of the one attempt anyone made on the cave. He came back alone, buys rounds for those who did not, and says only that it asked politely.

loreStory.t: What the whole country knows about him fits in
one chapter

: the summer morning, the best the fires had, the evening he came back out alone, unhollowed, unmarked, and the three words every asker since has been paid. This record will not improve on it. What it can add is the shape of his evenings. He buys rounds for people who are not there to drink them, and the ritual has an order: the same cups, the same places at the table, filled and left standing, and his own drunk last, facing the door.
People read the silence as a wound and grant it the wide berth wounds get.
Bettany

tested it. She asked him nothing about the inside — only about the ones who went in — and he talked until the candles were done: names, trades, who owed whom, who sang badly on the walk east, freely and warmly and in order. His account of that morning is the fullest thing in
the Chronicle
, and it stops at the mouth of the cave like a cut rope. A wound does not choose its edges that cleanly. A promise does.
What was promised, and to whom, is nowhere in this book, because he has kept it out of every book, and pays for the keeping in public and in small change: the rounds he cannot afford, the
eastern stone

sold under its price the same evening it was paid to him, the seat that faces the door. He could go on — he is as whole as the day he walked out, which is its own uncomfortable fact — and he stays, and keeps the cups filled, and lets everyone call it grief, because the truth has no polite shape: silence that is kept was silence given to someone, and Hearn is good for his debts.

characters.lore: Gunnar, a road-worn wanderer of Nangijala. Grey cloak, plain sword, no home worth naming. Passing through, as always.
characters.loreDesc: Wanderer. He maps the Drift with stakes and string, walks the eastern line every year, and has stopped telling anybody what the measurements say.
loreStory: Most people meet a Turn the morning after, when the path goes somewhere new. Gunnar meets it in the numbers. He walks the country with stakes and knotted string and a ledger of small tidy figures, re-measuring what everyone else re-remembers, and for years he did it out loud — sheets posted at the fires, a hamlet warned its ford was going, the shore people told which cliff not to build under. They thanked him and built there anyway, or moved and grumbled, and either way the maps did what maps are for.

loreStory.t: Then his eastern line began coming back wrong in one direction only. Soft ground — the kind that forgets faster than anyone is forgetting it — moving year on year, not wandering the way the Drift wanders but travelling, and travelling toward the meadow.
The Hole Under the Mountain
says he has stopped telling anybody what he measures, and it is so. The spring he was sure, he walked to the meadow fire, sat down across from
Solveig
, accepted the second cup, and talked for an hour about the weather. Then he thanked her and left. He has made that walk three springs running.

loreStory: His reasoning is as tidy as the ledger: a fright helps no one who cannot act on it; the fires cannot move a meadow; so the knowing should sit with the one man fit to carry it. That is also why he has never gone on — you cannot leave, he says, in the middle of a measurement. The flaw in the reasoning is not on his maps. It is in the man: he has mistaken carrying a thing alone for keeping people safe from it, and the ground is not slowing down.

characters.name: Jehanne
characters.lore: Jehanne, a priestess of Nangijala. Keeps the quiet rites nobody watches. Kind, and entirely unbudgeable.
characters.loreDesc: Priestess of a faith she no longer believes and cannot stop practising. Ask her and she will say so. Watch her hold a service and you will not believe her.

loreStory.t: The believing fell out of her somewhere on the crossing, and she will say so to anyone who asks, flat as a floorboard. Why she holds the services anyway is in
the Human Dead

, and it is the truth: the practice is a rota by another name, the candles are a fire, people come and stay and talk, and the talk is the thing. All of that she will admit in daylight. What she will not admit is what happens to her voice inside the service.

Ask her at the woodpile and the prayer goes to no one; ask her mid-liturgy and you would swear she had seen the answer. She never decided on the lie. It arrived like a work-skill, the way a smith's arm learns the blow: the old words want certainty behind them, and her body supplies it, and forty faces steady in the candlelight because the priest is sure. Last spring she sat with a friend at
Faded

— a woman losing the faces of her own children — who asked the bare question: will I be held? Jehanne heard her own voice say yes, whole and warm, not a splinter of doubt in it, and watched the woman settle under the word. It bought her a season. Jehanne walked home in the dark, was sick at the crossroads, and has never told anyone which part of the evening did that.

loreStory: She could go on; she is remembered whole by half the fireside, which is more than most can claim. She stays because the rota is short-handed, she says, and it is true, and it is not the reason. The reason is the forty faces. They believe her certainty, not her confession — and if she left, the leaving would tell them which one was real.

characters.lore: Bettany, a scribe of Nangijala. Keeps ledgers nobody reads until the day everybody does.
characters.loreDesc: Scribe of the Chronicle — the book in your hands. She began it the day her grief went missing, and she will not close it until she knows what took it.

loreStory.t: Britt was the younger by six years and the quicker by every measure that is fun at a fair, and the sisters sang in parts — Britt above, Bettany under — through every wash-day of two lifetimes, the living one and this one. What happened when Britt went on is told in
the Long Morning
, and Bettany would rather you read it there. The short of it: everyone the going-on bereaves loses the grief itself, and everyone but her has agreed to call that mercy.
In the back of
the Chronicle

, past the last written page, there is a private column of dates. On Britt's day each year Bettany sings both parts of the wash-song alone, her line and then her sister's — she has lost none of it, which is the whole horror — and waits to feel anything at all, and writes the result beside the date. The column is longer now than some chapters. Every entry says: still nothing. She is a careful scribe. If it ever says something else, she wants to know the day.
She interviews everyone who will sit, and most sit once.
Wendell

gets her a whole evening every week and believes it is for his east road, which she has duly saved — forty pages, milestone by milestone. She keeps coming for a different reason. Wendell met Britt once, at a shearing, and he tells it a little differently each time — the dress, the weather, what Britt called across the pen — and Bettany sits very still through every version, waiting for the one with something new in it. He knows exactly what he is doing. He spins that morning out a thread a week, because the evenings are what he is really trading for; she pays, and both of them let the price go on being called the road.

characters.name: Ivo

characters.name: Joss

objects.loreDesc: A stain is a story that ended at the nearest fire. Almost always.
loreStory: Fights end. The broken go down where they stand and, some hours on, stand up again beside the nearest tended fire, short a little of whatever they were thinking when it happened. That is the arithmetic of violence here: it costs a thought, not a life. So a stain on the stones is not a marker. It is the start of a story that finished somewhere warmer — an argument gone too far, a robbery on the road, a creature that had to be released the hard way — and by the time the rain gets around to it, the person it came out of has usually walked past it twice without looking down.

loreStory.t: Usually. The re-forming needs a tended fire, and the rota has lapsed almost everywhere. Out where the map has gone
Quiet
, the nearest fire can be a long way to nowhere. The old hands read stains the way trackers read prints: fresh means a scuffle. Faded, far from any light, means don't ask.

objects.loreDesc: The fire on the meadow. It has never once been let go out.

loreStory.t: It has never gone out. That is not a figure of speech: it is the fire Signe lit, or a fire fed from it, or a fire people only say was fed from it, and in this country all three are the same wood. Every soul that ever opened its eyes on the meadow saw this light first — before the stone house, before the grass, before their own name came back to them.
The waking
is cold and confused everywhere except within reach of it.
Solveig

keeps it now. There is a seat with its back to the wind, a second cup in case the newest arrival comes thirsty, and split wood stacked like a promise. When she asks your name and one true thing, look into the flames while you answer; everyone does. What is said there holds.

loreStory: Feed it if you pass. Not because it needs you tonight — because one night it will, and it does not announce which.

objects.name: Wooden grave cross
objects.description: a wooden grave cross that appears from the ground where something died

placement.note: Render the sprite scaled so its height == world_px_height; a character is character_height_px tall.

objects.loreDesc: A cross over no grave, raised for someone who never woke.
loreStory: Nothing is buried under it. Nothing is ever buried here: the Quiet leaves no body, no bone, no weight for a shovel. A grave is a living country's answer to a problem this one does not have.

loreStory.t: The crosses are for the other absence. People die together — a sickness, a wreck, a winter — and one of them wakes on the meadow and the other never comes.
The waking

owes no explanation and gives none. So the woken do the one thing left to do: they cut two pieces of wood, plant them where the missing one would have been welcome, and say the name aloud, on the old understanding that what is spoken holds. It is the only telling in Nangijala that does not work. The name holds nothing, because the person it belongs to is not here to be held. They say it anyway. Every cross on the map is somebody still saying it.

items.name: Amber Root
items.description: Hacked off a Stumpling's root-leg and glazed hard with amber sap. Warm to hold, and alchemists know it.

items.name: Hawk Feather
items.description: Barred brown with an olive tip, and too big for any bird anyone has flushed out of these woods yet.

items.name: Obsidian
items.description: Fist-sized lump of glossy black glass, cooled out of some fire-thing's crust. Keen enough to shave with, so don't.

items.name: Black Glass
items.description: Slab of black volcanic glass, faceted and chipped. It sheds off a Magmashell's plates as the fire cools.

items.name: Onyx Shard
items.description: Wedge of near-black glass with a cold blue sheen, cracked out of Rimeshard's rock. The edge never dulls.

items.name: Rib Cage
items.description: Spine and curved ribs, bleached clean. A Palehusk wore it badly, and a Glowbone would have lit it up.

items.name: Sea Shells
items.description: Scallops and spirals, sun-faded to tan. The tide made them, and the swamp does nothing but carry them about.

items.name: Rift Geode
items.description: Split grey stone bleeding cold cyan light from every seam. Golems grow around them and resent the loss.

items.name: Beast Tooth
items.description: Thumb-long ivory with a notched crown. A Palemaw bites once; a Diretusk never has to. Both leave these.

items.name: Grave Dirt
items.description: Crumbly dark earth studded with bone chips. Whatever the Palehusk climbed out of, it brought some along.

items.name: Root Bundle
items.description: Brown roots tied off with twine and dried brittle. Whatever woodland lump was hauling it does not want it back.

items.name: Plume Bundle
items.description: Green, teal, blue and red plumes lashed to a cord. Nothing in these woods wears feathers like that.

items.name: Broken Tusk
items.description: Snapped off at the root, cream shading to brown. The Diretusk it belonged to never broke stride.

items.name: Bronze Knife
items.description: Camp bronze on a ribbed wooden grip, made for rope and rations. The Nightmule that hauled it went feral first.

items.name: Quartz Shard
items.description: Prised out of Mosscairn rubble and Rimeshard ice alike: one six-sided white point ringed with chippings.

items.name: Stone Egg
items.description: Fitted stone plates packed into an oval, shaken loose from a Magmashell. Nothing has ever hatched out of one.

items.name: Coiled Rope
items.description: Braided tan hemp, chewed to a splay at one end by a Nightmule with opinions. Still holds a knot, mostly.

items.name: Magma Stone
items.description: Faceted like an egg, orange over deep red and split with glowing seams. Fire-things leak these when they crack.

items.name: Bone Talon
items.description: Hooked grey bone, thick and cracked at the base. Fiends and the glowing dead shed them, and the point stays keen.

items.name: Crab Pincer
items.description: Brown, jointed and hooked at the tip. Whatever the swamp blobs swallowed to get it went down sideways.

items.name: Curved Fang
items.description: White ivory going tan at the root, worn fine by use. Cave-jaws and dusk-hunters both leave these behind.

items.name: Bat Wing
items.description: Dark membrane on thin bone struts, folded shut. Leathery, and off nothing anyone has cornered yet.

items.name: Oak Plank
items.description: Planed dark oak, the grain unmistakable, knocked out of a Stumpling. It walked once, and now it holds shelves.

items.name: Dry Grass
items.description: Olive stalks tied off with cord, hauled out of a meadow nest. Poor fodder, but it burns beautifully.

items.name: Rune Locket
items.description: Oval bronze, knotted with spirals nobody reads aloud twice. The Palehusk wore it under skin that was not its own.

items.name: Ember Shard
items.description: Leaf-shaped crystal veined orange and red. It stays warm in the pouch, like the shell it was prised from.

items.name: Gilded Fang
items.description: Someone gilded a hunter's tooth, hollow at the root and polished bright. Nobody asks whose mouth it left.

items.name: Husked Nuts
items.description: Hard glossy kernels streaked tan and brown, a good fistful. Small woodland things hoard them, and now so do you.

items.name: Mandrake
items.description: A knobbly root with legs of its own and a wilted crown. The Stumpling was carrying it, or it was family.

items.name: Gold Ore
items.description: Rubble-grade rock studded with raw gold. It was a Mosscairn's shoulder until you argued about ownership.

items.name: Amber Fang
items.description: Broad amber-yellow tooth, split from crown to root. Even an Emberjaw loses one on the wrong kind of bone.

items.name: Jade Shard
items.description: Teal-green crystal with a wicked point, prised out of a Mosscairn's seams. Holds an edge and a grudge.

items.name: Herb Bundle
items.description: Long green stalks tied into a sheaf, damp from the ditch some blob had been squatting in.

items.name: Green Slime
items.description: Half a pond-dweller, domed and translucent, still faintly warm. Alchemists want it and will not say why.

items.name: Rock Pile
items.description: Rounded brown stones in a heap, which is all a Mosscairn amounts to once the magic stops holding it together.

items.name: Sage Leaves
items.description: Bitter grey-green leaves off the meadow scrub. Good in stew, better in poultices, fatal by the handful.

items.name: Iron Chain
items.description: Three pitted iron links, worn smooth where a harness rubbed. The Nightmule that wore it is still out there.

items.name: Hooked Wing
items.description: Leathery brown membrane on finger-bones, with a claw at the crown. Whatever flies on these keeps to its cave.

items.name: Nacre Shard
items.description: Turn this flake of shell and it shifts green to violet. Nothing shelled enough to grow one lives here yet.

items.name: Ivory Talon
items.description: Cream-white and curved to a needle point, the socket left ragged. Glowbones and Frostwraiths grow them in sets.

items.name: Great Pearl
items.description: One flawless sphere, off-white with a lilac sheen. Nobody will say which water it was brought up out of.

items.name: Thread Spool
items.description: Half a spool of plain linen thread. Something stitched the Palehusk together, and it was not a tailor.

items.name: Loose Teeth
items.description: Molars, curved fangs and small incisors, no two from the same jaw. Palemaws and Emberjaws shed them constantly.

items.name: Matted Pelt
items.description: Coarse black fur clumped and matted, with stray quills caught in it. Something out there is patchy now.

items.name: Mint Slime
items.description: Mint-green, translucent, and lit by a pale core. Every pond blob in the valley leaves one behind, wobbling.

items.name: Driftwood
items.description: Grey, water-worn branches still furred with moss. Cut a Stumpling down and this is most of what is left.

items.name: Watcher Mask
items.description: Grim steel with cheek guards and a third eye graven above the slits. The fiends that wore it had spares.

items.name: Beast Molars
items.description: Two grinders with forked roots, one big enough for a Diretusk. Both chewed harder things than grass.

items.name: Shadow Claw
items.description: A matched pair of glossy black hooks, sharp as the day they grew. Duskfang and its cousins do not give them up.

items.name: Bone Beetle
items.description: Palm-sized and bone-pale, its plated back mottled tan, six legs tucked under. The valley's small fry all carry one.

items.name: Pale Wing
items.description: Tan membrane on pale finger bones, torn free mid-flight. The gaunt things that haunt the drifts fly on these.

items.name: Frost Quartz
items.description: Ice-blue spires on a common base, cold indoors and out. Rimeshard grows this in its rock and swings the rest.

items.name: Rime Stones
items.description: Blue-white pebbles, a good dozen, that will not melt in the palm. Whatever a Frostling is packed from, this is it.

items.name: Moth Wing
items.description: Pale tan and ribbed brown, with a blue sheen at the base. Something big and soft-winged shed it in the dark.

items.name: Ivory Horns
items.description: Four ivory horns splayed from one base, ridged like bark. Fiends and wraiths grow them for arguments they win.

items.name: Silk Skein
items.description: Silvery cord wound tight and bound at the waist, cool to the touch. No hand in Nangijala spun this one.

items.name: Hornet Nest
items.description: Tan paper in banded layers, one dark doorway low on the side. Prised out of a Stumpling's moss, and empty. Mostly.

items.name: Pitted Ring
items.description: Thick hammered silver, tarnished and pitted all over, off a Palehusk's borrowed finger. It fits nobody at all.

items.name: Beast Eye
items.description: Whole and damp, a brown iris in a veined tan ball. The fiends that carry spares will not miss this one.

items.name: Iris Petals
items.description: Purple petals with pale wedged stems, gathered past bloom. Meadow blobs trail them wherever they bounce.

items.name: Venom Claw
items.description: Pulled from an Ashfiend before it crumbled. The purple hook is fine, but the green crust on the tip is not.
items.loreDesc: A purple hook with one pale ridge of light down the curve, and a hard green crust dried on the last third of the point.

loreStory.t: It grew where it sits — the one thing off an
Ashfiend

that did. Longer than a finger, curved well past use, the base a socket shaped around a knuckle that is not there any more. Hafted, it makes a poor knife every time, and people keep the poor knife, because a claw is worth little and a claw with a hand behind it is worth something.

loreStory: The crust on the point is the part worth money: mustard at its base, hard green at the tip, sitting on the purple rather than in it. It was put there; it did not grow there. It flakes under a thumbnail, so the careful carry one point-down in a stiff wrap and wash afterwards.

loreStory.t: Bettany
pays over the odds for a well-crusted one, and she is not buying knives. The same green comes off
the pale walking thing
on the black rock, and two creatures' leavings agreeing about a pigment is the kind of sentence
the Chronicle

exists to catch. Whether this point put the green into something or drew it out, the crust will not say. She keeps her best one wrapped in linen inside a chapter that has no words in it yet — just the claw, and a heading: which way did it run.

items.name: Prism Plume
items.description: Banded blue through green to red down a tan quill. Whatever grew a tail of these has not shown itself yet.

items.name: Raw Meat
items.description: Thick, red, rimmed with brown fat. Which beast it came off is between you, the cook, and nobody else.

items.name: Cloth Roll
items.description: Coarse grey canvas off a Nightmule's pack, rolled tight and trailing a tail. Tents do not sew themselves.

items.name: Rough Stone
items.description: Cracked brown rock with flat faceted sides. Half the things that shed it were walking around a moment ago.

items.name: Clawed Foot
items.description: Three cream claws on a brown scaled foot, cut clean at the joint. An Emberjaw's still holds its heat.

items.name: Scaled Paw
items.description: Mottled grey-green hide and three pale curled claws. A Palemaw leaves them, and never in matching pairs.

items.name: River Stone
items.description: Worn smooth, grey-blue and cold in the palm. Every pond blob keeps one, and none of them will say why.

items.name: Snow Tuft
items.description: A burr of white fur bristling every way, blue in its shadows. Warm to wear, and slow to finish thawing.

items.name: Gloom Cap
items.description: Fat violet cap, pale freckles, thick lavender stem. It grows on Stumplings, which should tell you plenty.

items.name: Marrow Bone
items.description: Knobbed at both ends and stained where beige should not be. A Palemaw was busy with it before you were.

items.name: Rough Hide
items.description: Pegged square with little wooden stakes, edges left ragged. Somebody began the tanning and gave up on it.

items.name: Teal Quill
items.description: Teal at the base, gold at the tip, and light as nothing. Scribes want the bird; nobody has found the bird.

items.name: Bone Bundle
items.description: Long pale bones tied off in a bundle. A Palehusk was carrying them, which raises questions about the string.

items.name: Tooth Ridge
items.description: Ivory cones socketed in a slab of jawbone, unblunted. Whatever carried it never needed a second bite.

items.name: Twig Skimmer
items.description: Four glassy wings over a body like a snapped twig. Shaken loose from whatever swamp thing you flattened.

items.name: Yellow Molar
items.description: Thumb-sized, yellowed and worn flat. Grinding teeth like this come out of things that chew all day.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Violet facets around a gold rune, cut from an Emberwing. Hits land arcane, and spells come back to hand faster.

soul.power: +20 arcane damage on hit and -10% spell cooldowns

items.loreDesc: Faceted violet, plum deepening to lilac, with a thumbnail of gold at the middle that looks written rather than grown.

loreStory.t: Every facet on one is a one-off; the mark is not. Two strokes and a splayed foot, in gold, small enough to hide under a thumbnail, identical down to the stroke on every stone ever brought in. Off a creature that is
nothing but retellings

, the piece that pressed hardest was the one thing all its tellers' countries remember alike: gold, which does not drift. Set in a blade it lends tempo — the stroke arrives as if it had been made once already.
The mark is also why it is the most forged stone on any bench. Violet glass lumps well, and a forger with real gold gets the mark right every time, gold being the point of gold.
Osric
, new enough to still count in living years, bought one cheap off a stranger at his first market and carried it to
Sigrun

for setting. She drew it once through her hearth ash and handed it back grey. Ash will not sit on a true one — one wipe and it is finished — and the glass kept its coat. It hangs over his forge door now with the price scratched underneath, and he takes the ribbing better than he would take the sympathy.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Dark banded stone lined with living gold, pulled from a Glowbone. Burns with light, and nearby undead go blind.

soul.power: +20 radiant damage on hit and blinds undead within three tiles

items.loreDesc: Dark stone terraced in bands, a seam of live gold running the length of them. It lights whatever pouch you put it in.
loreStory: The smiths' rule with this one: never on the bench after dark. The seam is live, and beside heated metal there is no telling the colour of the work from the colour coming off the stone, so settings happen at noon with the doors open, by people who otherwise keep their doors shut to read the heat.

loreStory.t: It does not go down when you put it away, which is why you cannot carry one and also arrive anywhere unannounced — and why, when the fire on the east road lapsed, its last keeper left a banded stone glowing on the sill as she went, so the road would think the light was still kept.
Wendell

walked that road while the trick still worked. He says you could tell a mile off, because a fire moves and a stone only glows. He stopped anyway, both ways, sat down on the step, and told it what he had seen on the road lately. It seemed wrong to pass a kept light without paying for it.
What bothers people is that it lends the whole light, undiminished, out of a lump a hand closes around. As if
the creature it comes off
was never lit through at all — as if the light was always this small, and the body was built around it for carrying.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Charred black, cracked open by molten veins. Magmashell's banked fire, and it leaves what you hit burning.

soul.power: +14 fire damage on hit and sets targets burning for 3s

items.loreDesc: Charred black plates forked open by live orange veins that never cool. What you strike goes on burning after you stop.
loreStory: Ask somebody who carries one what they carry it in and you get a considered answer. Cloth chars through in a season; a pouch comes back stiff as a boot dried too near the hearth. Most end at a tin of sand lashed outside the pack, where the thing that cannot be persuaded to stop can do the least.

That is also what it does off an edge. Most fire is over when the swing is; this one is left behind, still burning after you step back. What got pressed to make it was never flame — it was the banking: heat held in, year after year, no fuel, no audience, no occasion. A thing like that does not learn to finish just because you have.

loreStory.t: Few ever come to hand, since a crossing has to empty first, and the one
Magmashell
anyone can still visit shows no sign of obliging. A collector once offered
Gunnar

good gold to stop paying its pause — one regular fewer, one crossing nearer done. Gunnar quoted back the number of years he has walked it, and the collector could not tell whether that was a price or a warning. Neither has anyone since.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Blue slate cracked around a cold white star. Nobody has found what grows these, only that they frost a blade.

soul.power: +9 frost damage and slows struck targets by 25%

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Dull brown plates veined with copper, left by a Puddling. Thickens armor and roots you where you stand.

soul.power: +12 armor and 15% knockback resistance

items.loreDesc: Dull brown plates shut on a copper vein, far too heavy for its size. A Puddling's last piece; in armour, hard to shift.
loreStory: The one they put in a new hand first. It weighs wrong — not heavy, wrongly heavy, in a way the arm reports before the eye agrees. Armour set with one does the same trick at scale: the blow that should have put you on your back leaves you standing where you were, and you find out afterwards. Wearers call it the least dramatic advantage in the trade, and keep wearing it.

loreStory.t: The trouble is the count. Every hard piece is supposed to be
the bottom of one long forgetting
, and the wet ground gives up more of these than the low country has lives to account for, by a margin that worsens every season.
Wendell
says that in his day the count came out even. Wendell says that about most counts.

loreStory: The sorters keep three explanations in stock. That the ground itself is doing the forgetting, and the wet places are where it runs deepest. That the counting was always sloppy. And a third, said late in the evening and not repeated in daylight: that the arithmetic is fine, and it is the assumption of one life to one stone that is wrong.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Packed grey-green cobbles with no light left in them. Its creature is still unmet, and blows slide past whoever holds it.

soul.power: +8% dodge chance and attackers miss more often in dim light

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Mossy green split by a red vein, cut from a Stumpling. It hits harder and feeds the wound back to you.

soul.power: +9 damage on hit and heals you for 8% of damage dealt

items.loreDesc: Moss green blotched with bark brown, dark veins branching in to one red knot at the middle. Filed with the blood stones.
loreStory: In a full bag you can find one without looking. Every hard piece is warm; this one is warm unevenly, a hot spot over the red knot at the middle, the way heat comes through a coat with somebody in it. Collectors mention that to each other exactly once, at the start, and not again.

loreStory.t: Every one of these on a bench was cracked out of
a Stumpling
by a hand other than
Sigrun's

; her refusal is its own story. What her bench shows is the other half of it: she will set the stones once the cracking is done elsewhere — sets them better than anyone in the district — and she lifts each one from the tray with the long tongs she otherwise keeps for iron out of the fire.

loreStory: An apprentice asked about the tongs once, it being a cold stone by iron's standards. It is warm in the middle, she said. They are all warm, said the apprentice, which is true. Not like this, she said, and got on with the setting, and the apprentice put the question away with the other things you do not ask Sigrun twice.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Plated grey rock split by a bright cyan seam of Rimeshard ice. In a blade it bites deep frost and leaves the target wading.

soul.power: +16 frost damage on hit and slows the target by 30% for 3 seconds

items.loreDesc: Grey plates split by one bright cyan seam that runs clean through. It bites frost, and what it strikes runs late.

loreStory.t: Warm, which is the first surprise — off the crystal ground, out of a shape that is ice from the crown down, and it sits in the palm at blood heat, the seam warmest of all. The sorters point to that when asked whether anything in a
Rimeshard
was ever under way at all: watched from a ridge it might as well be weather, and weather does not leave a warm stone.

loreStory: The grading is done on the seam, not on either material. Sight along it: on a good one the cyan enters one face and comes out the other, clean through. On a poor one it stops inside, and what you own is a grey pebble with a stripe. The rock alone is worth nothing; the ice alone is worth nothing; the join is the worth.

loreStory.t: New hands find that funny for about a week.
Osric

did not laugh at all. He is a smith; a join that outvalues both its pieces was the first price in this country that struck him as honestly arrived at, and he paid it without haggling, which the stone-sellers still bring up.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Pebbled black stone veined in cyan, the storm inside a Frostwraith. Its lightning strikes, then jumps to the next body.

soul.power: +15 lightning damage with a 20% chance to chain to a second target

items.loreDesc: Pebbled black under a net of branching cyan that will not sit still. Warm. Its spark rarely stops at one body.
